security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU TCG or helper code inverts the tagcheck-exempt page condition when deciding whether to perform MTE tag checks on a regular load/store — i.e., it performs tag checks when the instruction page IS tagcheck-exempt (and skips them when the page is NOT exempt), matching the pre-fix spec text with the missing negation
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: riscv_mte_tag_check_needed|tagcheck_exempt.*tag_check|check_tag.*exempt|mte_tag_check.*page.*exempt — any function or branch that gates tag-check execution on the exempt status of the instruction page, where the boolean sense may be inverted
security_spec.summary: Inverted tagcheck-exempt page condition causes QEMU to skip tag checks on non-exempt code (guest bypasses MTE protections) and fault on exempt code (spurious tag violations), breaking the kernel's memory-safety enforcement

findings.finding: The RISC-V MTE tag-check gating code (riscv_mte_tag_check_needed, tagcheck_exempt-based tag-check decision, etc.) does not exist in this QEMU version. There is no code to invert the boolean sense of the tagcheck-exempt condition, so the vulnerability pattern cannot be present. The PR's IOMMU change (riscv-iommu.c:750-756) is an unrelated MSI page table pointer validation check.
findings.snippet: No tag-check-exempt code found; all MTE tag-checking logic exists only in target/arm/, not in target/riscv/.
